html:
The Jupaú, better known as the Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau, are a small Tupi-Kawahiva people of the forests of central Rondônia in western Brazil. Their language is close to those of other Kawahiva peoples such as the Parintintin and Tenharim, and part of the same family as the old coastal Tupi.

Brazilian government agents first made peaceful contact with them in 1981, as roads and settlers poured into Rondônia. Epidemics followed and killed many. Their territory was marked out in 1991, but loggers, miners and land grabbers keep invading it. Their fight to defend it is the subject of the 2022 documentary The Territory.
